With a=EJ, b=E[J(J-1)], m(0)=1=f(0)+1, the moment equations m’=am and f’=a f+(2a+b)m² give m=θ^-a and Var=(1+b/a)m(m-1)=(EJ²/EJ)m(m-1). The pointwise integer inequality (j-q)(j-q-1)>=0 yields EJ²>=a²+δ(1-δ), unique adjacent support equality. For a>1 the {1,M} laws with mean a have unbounded second moments as M→∞; mean-preserving mixing realizes each finite κ above the floor. At a=1, J=1 uniquely. Independent rational-moment checks corroborate exact equality examples. The external theorem associating a positive-integer dual law to the semigroup is a clearly identified premise; direct full-text access to its 2026 source was unavailable.
